## Proof

We claim **x = y**.

Suppose for contradiction that x ≠ y. Then z := x − y ≠ 0, so ‖z‖ > 0.

By the Hahn–Banach theorem, there exists a bounded linear functional T ∈ X* such that

$$T(z) = \|z\| \quad \text{and} \quad \|T\| = 1.$$

Concretely: define the linear functional on the one-dimensional subspace $\mathrm{span}\{z\}$ by $f(\alpha z) = \alpha\|z\|$, so $f(z)=\|z\|$ and $\|f\|=1$ on this subspace. By Hahn–Banach (norm-preserving extension), $f$ extends to some $T \in X^*$ with $\|T\|=1$ and $T(z)=\|z\|$.

Since $\|z\|>0$, we have $T(z) = T(x)-T(y) = \|z\| \neq 0$, hence $T(x) \neq T(y)$.

This contradicts the hypothesis that $T(x)=T(y)$ for all $T\in X^*$. Therefore the assumption $x\neq y$ is false, and

$$x = y.$$

### PROOF COMPLETE
